tex_content.html:
Corollary
[Formulas for the Levi-Civita Connection] ↗ prop:torsion-tensor ↗ prop:characterizations-of-metric-connections ↗ prob:torsion-tensor 1. ch5:5.11

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary, and let $ abla $ be its Levi-Civita connection.

  1. For smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$,

    egin{equation} \langle abla _XY,Z angle = rac12 igl(X\langle Y,Z angle +Y\langle Z,X angle -Z\langle X,Y angle -\langle Y,[X,Z] angle -\langle Z,[Y,X] angle +\langle X,[Z,Y] angle igr). ag {5.9} \end{equation}

    This is Koszul’s formula.

  2. In smooth coordinates,

    egin{equation} \Gamma ^k_{ij} = rac12g^{kl}(\partial _ig_{jl}+\partial _jg_{il}-\partial _lg_{ij}). ag {5.10} \end{equation}

  3. For a smooth local frame $(E_i)$, define $c^k_{ij}$ by

    egin{equation} [E_i,E_j]=c^k_{ij}E_k. ag {5.11} \end{equation}

    Then

    egin{equation} \Gamma ^k_{ij} = rac12g^{kl}\left(E_ig_{jl}+E_jg_{il}-E_lg_{ij} -g_{jm}c^m_{il}-g_{lm}c^m_{ji}+g_{im}c^m_{lj} ight). ag {5.12} \end{equation}

  4. If $g$ is Riemannian and $(E_i)$ is orthonormal, then

    egin{equation} \Gamma ^k_{ij}= rac12(c^k_{ij}-c^j_{ik}-c^i_{jk}). ag {5.13} \end{equation}

Proof

\sketch Formulas (5.9) and (5.10) follow from the theorem. Substituting $X=E_i$, $Y=E_j$, and $Z=E_l$ into (5.9) gives

\[ \Gamma ^q_{ij}g_{ql} = rac12\left(E_ig_{jl}+E_jg_{il}-E_lg_{ij} -g_{jm}c^m_{il}-g_{lm}c^m_{ji}+g_{im}c^m_{lj} ight). \]

Multiplication by $g^{kl}$ proves (5.12). If $g_{ij}=\delta _{ij}$, this reduces to (5.13), using antisymmetry of $c^k_{ij}$ in $i,j$.

□

Henceforth, geodesics are taken with respect to the Levi-Civita connection. Its coordinate coefficients (5.10) are the Christoffel symbols of $g$.
